next.connections.svc.steps.oauth1: Press «Sign in with {name}»: the service's page opens in a new window.
next.connections.svc.steps.oauth2: Sign in there and allow access for the agent.
next.connections.svc.steps.oauth3: The window closes by itself and the tools of the server appear here.
next.connections.svc.steps.token1: Press «Create token»: the service opens the page where the token is made.
next.connections.svc.steps.token2: Copy the token, paste it below and press Connect.
next.connections.svc.steps.tokenNoLink: Make a token or an API key in your account of the service and copy it.
next.connections.svc.steps.keys: Get the keys on the service's page (the links are under the steps) and copy them.
next.connections.svc.steps.keysNoLink: Get the keys in your account of the service and copy them.
next.connections.svc.steps.keysPaste: Paste them below and press Connect.
next.connections.svc.steps.none: The server needs no sign-in: press Connect.
next.connections.svc.own: A server of your own, by its address
next.connections.own.title: Your own service
next.connections.own.lead: The company's internal API, a self-made MCP server, any service that is not in the catalog. The agent finds out what it is from its address or docs, tries it, writes the description and asks for the key through the safe; you only agree on a card.
next.connections.own.name: Name
next.connections.own.checkHint: A GET that answers 2xx once the key is right
next.connections.own.apiNote: The key goes to this machine's safe and is never shown in an answer. An API with several keys, a key in the address or an OpenAPI file is easier to connect with the agent.
next.connections.own.commandHint: npx -y package@1.2.3 or uvx package==1.2.3: the version is exact
next.connections.own.localYes: I understand: this downloads and runs someone else's code on this machine, and it gets the keys I type
next.connections.own.can: What an agent can do with it
next.connections.own.draft:
Connect my own service to harnessly. Its address or documentation (an OpenAPI file will do): <paste the link here>.

Find out what kind of service it is (an MCP server, an API, a local server), try it, describe it and add it with connection_add. If it needs a key, ask for it with a card of the safe (harnessly secret ask), not in the chat.
